tasks.title: A known-issues page that stays current
requirements: docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md lists every open issue labelled bug and every limit the docs state (a sentence carrying the marker <!-- limit -->), each with its link or page, the date it was first seen and the workaround if there is one

scripts/docs/known-issues.mjs --check reads the open issues through the GitHub API (or a file given with --issues, for tests) and the docs, and fails naming any open bug or stated limit the page lacks and any listed issue that is closed; CI runs it on a schedule and before a release
the README and the docs index link the page

criteria.statement: SR-2.10 known issues: with a fixture issue list holding an open bug the page lacks, --check fails naming it; with a closed issue still listed, it fails; with a stated limit missing from the page, it fails; with the page complete, it passes

verifier.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='^SR-2.10 known issues' test/known-issues.test.mjs 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -30; [ $rc -eq 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -v pat='^SR-2.10 known issues$' 'BEGIN { n = split(pat, alt, "|") } function flush(  i) { if (cand != "") for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (cand ~ alt[i]) hit[i] = 1; cand = "" } /^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - / { flush(); name = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - /, "", name); if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*ok / && name !~ /# (SKIP|TODO)/ && name !~ /\.test\.m?js$/) cand = name; next } /^[[:space:]]*type: .suite./ { cand = "" } END { flush(); for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (!hit[i]) exit 1; exit 0 }'

tasks.title: A three-day soak of the free tier
requirements: scripts/soak/free-tier.mjs runs one vault for 72 hours on one machine: the daemon, GitHub backup to a local bare repository, the hooks of two clients driven at a fixed rate (remember, recall, the prompt hook, session end), a daemon restart every 6 hours and a network drop every hour

it writes bench/results/<date>-soak-<cpu>.json with the hardware, the hours run, the notes written and found again, notes_lost, daemon crashes, the hourly p95 of the prompt hook and of recall, and the hourly heap and disk use
a 10-minute form (--minutes 10) runs in CI on a schedule, so the script cannot rot

criteria.statement: SR-2.10 soak: the soak's one-minute form on a temp vault writes a results file with every field; a note deleted from the vault mid-run makes it report notes_lost 1 and exit non-zero
